title: Bucketed checkpoint compression and scratch defragmenter to reduce transient GPU working set
author: Anika Shah
release_notes: Reduced peak GPU working set via on-the-fly checkpoint compression and proactive scratch defragmentation; no public API changes.
description: Motivation: Production workloads show short-lived but high transient GPU allocations caused by activation checkpoint snapshots and fragmented scratch buffers. This increases required capacity and forces conservative autoscaling. This PR implements a two-pronged runtime optimization: 1) bucketed, lossy-aware checkpoint compression for transient activation snapshots to shrink per-request checkpoint workspace; 2) an epochal scratch defragmenter that compacts free regions between request epochs and cooperates with the continuous batcher to avoid mid-batch relocations. Both features are runtime-configurable and avoid changing model artifacts.
commits: 9f2a4b6: introduce bucketed checkpoint compressor with zstd-compatible streaming format
21e7c3d: add per-bucket entropy estimator and selective lossy thresholds
c3b7f8a: implement scratch defragmenter and epoch markers in the batcher
d45e91b: KV cache hotset tracker + compaction hook to reclaim redundant slots
f8b2a11: add unit and integration tests for compressed snapshot compatibility
a12c334: docs: performance notes and tuning knobs
b9d4e22: perf: tune kernel selection to prefer low-memory variants when compressed snapshots in-flight
diff_summary: ~ introduce compressor and defragmenter modules, modify batcher to emit epoch markers, add KV compaction hook, update kernel selector to prefer low-memory kernels when compressed checkpoints present; ~1400 additions, ~620 deletions
performance_impact: Benchmark summary: peak GPU memory reduced 18-26% on representative chat and generation workloads (seq_len 1024/2048), end-to-end throughput improved 6-10% for latency-insensitive batch workloads; median p50 latency unchanged, p99 latency reduced slightly on heavy memory pressure scenarios.
safety_and_compatibility: Compatibility: compressed snapshots are only used for transient checkpoint workspace (not persisted model artifacts). There is a runtime flag to disable compression per-customer. Backwards compatibility: server can accept compressed snapshots produced by older binaries; tests added to validate cross-version decompression.
tuning_knobs: Runtime knobs added: runtime.checkpoint.bucket_sizes (comma list), runtime.checkpoint.lossy_threshold_pct (0-100), runtime.scratch.defrag_epoch_ms, runtime.kv.compact_hotset_window, runtime.kernel.prefer_low_memory_when_ckpt
manual_test_steps: 1) Start local dev runtime with DEBUG ckpt logging enabled. 2) Run tests/perf/benchmark_bucketed_ckpt.yml with and without compression flag. 3) Observe reduced transient allocations via /metrics and CUDA memory sampler. 4) Toggle defragmenter and run long-lived batched workload to assert no mid-batch relocations.
review_conversation: Miguel Torres: High-level this looks solid. Could you justify the 5% default lossy threshold? Need signal on when to fall back to lossless.
Anika Shah: Response: 5% was chosen after offline eval (see docs/perf) — we fall back to lossless for buckets whose entropy estimate is >0.92; added unit tests to validate fallback logic.
Priya Raman: CI flaked on perf-tests initially; please add guard to skip long perf job in PR CI and run in nightly. Also confirm telemetry for compressed vs uncompressed snapshot counts.

Ethan Cole: Minor nit: kernel selector change should be opt-in per-deployment. Could we gate behind runtime.kernel.prefer_low_memory_when_ckpt?
Anika Shah: Done — introduced the runtime knob and documented behavior in kernel_selector.cpp comments.
